source.publication: 2025 IT-511 Individual Income Tax Booklet (Georgia DOR), with Form 500 and Schedule 1 bound in (PDF pages 41-49)
source.section: Subtractions item 1 'Retirement income' (PDF p.21); Retirement Income Exclusion notes (PDF p.24: Social Security, Railroad Retirement and exempt income left out; items allocated to the owner); Schedule 1 page 2 lines 1-17 and footnote (PDF p.48; 2025GA500.pdf p.8): lines 1-5 earned income limited to the 5,000 Maximum Earned Income, lines 6-14 unearned retirement income, line 16 maximum allowable exclusion 35,000 (62-64) or 65,000 (65 or older), line 17 the lesser of lines 15 and 16; Subtractions item 5 'Social Security or Railroad Retirement (Tier 1 and Tier 2) paid by the Railroad Retirement Board included in Federal adjusted gross income' (PDF p.22); Schedule 1 line 8 (PDF p.47); DOR Retirees FAQ ('Taxable Social Security and Railroad Retirement on the Federal return are exempt'); Form 500 lines 8-16 (booklet PDF pp.16-17: Line 8 federal AGI, Line 10 Georgia AGI, Line 11 standard deduction, Lines 13-15c, Line 16 'Multiply the amount on Line 15c by 5.19%. Round to nearest dollar.'); Form 500 Schedule 1 page 1 lines 1-14 (PDF p.47); rate cite PDF p.9 What's New; standard deduction cite PDF p.16 Line 11

worked: Federal AGI = wages 20,000.00 + Georgia public pension 30,000.00 + IRA distribution 20,000.00 + taxable Social Security 25,500.00 (gross Social Security 30,000.00; the federal taxable part is given as 25,500.00, 85%) = 95,500.00. Federal taxable income = 95,500.00 - (standard deduction 15,750.00 + 2,000.00 x 1 aged 65 or older) = 77,750.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; federal figures are given, not tested; Georgia starts from federal AGI). Schedule 1 line 8 Social Security, the taxable portion from the federal return, 25,500.00, subtracted in full. Schedule 1 page 2 (taxpayer, age 70; Social Security is left out of the worksheet, PDF p.24): line 1 salary and wages 20,000.00; line 2 other earned income 0.00; line 3 total earned income 20,000.00; line 4 maximum earned income 5,000.00; line 5 lesser of lines 3 and 4 = 5,000.00; line 11 taxable IRA distributions 20,000.00, line 12 taxable pensions 30,000.00; line 14 = 50,000.00; line 15 = 5,000.00 + 50,000.00 = 55,000.00; line 16 maximum allowable exclusion 65,000.00; line 17 lesser of lines 15 and 16 = 55,000.00. Below the 65,000 cap; only 5,000 of the 20,000 of wages counts. Schedule 1 additions lines 1-5 none, line 6 = 0.00. Schedule 1 line 13 total subtractions = line 7a retirement income exclusion 55,000.00 + line 8 Social Security 25,500.00 = 80,500.00; line 14 net adjustments = 0.00 - 80,500.00 = -80,500.00. Form 500 line 8 federal AGI 95,500.00; line 9 = -80,500.00; line 10 Georgia AGI = 95,500.00 - 80,500.00 = 15,000.00. Line 11 standard deduction (single) 12,000.00 (the filer takes the federal standard deduction, so must take Georgia's); line 13 = 15,000.00 - 12,000.00 = 3,000.00; line 14 dependent exemption 0 dependents = 0.00; line 15a = 3,000.00; line 15b NOL 0.00; line 15c = 3,000.00. Line 16 tax = 5.19% x 3,000.00 = 155.7000 = 155.70; the form rounds to the nearest dollar and gives 156; expected uses the unrounded formula to the cent. Line 17 Low Income Credit: federal AGI is not under 20,000, so none; no other credits; credits 0.00; state income tax = 155.70.
